sections.heading: Section 1: Vector Spaces and Linear Combinations

questions.q: Given word vectors $\mathbf{u} = [2, -1, 3]^T$ and $\mathbf{v} = [1, 4, -2]^T$, compute the linear combination $3\mathbf{u} - 2\mathbf{v}$.
Two embedding vectors $\mathbf{a} = [k, 2, -1]^T$ and $\mathbf{b} = [3, -4, 2]^T$ are orthogonal in semantic space. Find the value of $k$.
Determine whether the three feature vectors $\mathbf{v}_1 = [1, 0]^T$, $\mathbf{v}_2 = [0, 1]^T$, and $\mathbf{v}_3 = [3, -2]^T$ are linearly independent in $\mathbf{R}^2$.
choices: Linearly dependent (any set of $>2$ vectors in $\mathbf{R}^2$ is dependent)
Cannot be determined without a matrix inversion
questions.answer: Since the dimension of the space is 2, any collection of 3 vectors is linearly dependent: $\mathbf{v}_3 = 3\mathbf{v}_1 - 2\mathbf{v}_2$.

questions.q: Calculate the Manhattan ($L_1$) norm and Euclidean ($L_2$) norm of the embedding error vector $\mathbf{e} = [3, -4, 12]^T$.
Find the Chebyshev ($L_\infty$) norm of the parameter vector $\mathbf{w} = [-7, 2, 5, -9, 4]^T$.
In Lasso regression, why does adding an $L_1$ penalty to the loss function induce exact feature sparsity (weights driven to 0)?
choices: The diamond-shaped $L_1$ contour has sharp corners on the coordinate axes
The $L_1$ norm is continuously differentiable everywhere
The $L_1$ penalty penalizes large weights much more heavily than $L_2$
The $L_1$ norm computes the determinant of the covariance matrix
questions.answer: The level sets of the $L_1$ ball are non-smooth polytopes with vertices on the axes, where elliptical loss contours naturally contact first.

sections.heading: Section 3: Dot Products, Cosine Similarity and Angular Distance

questions.q: Two query embeddings are $\mathbf{u} = [1, 1, 0]^T$ and $\mathbf{v} = [0, 2, 2]^T$. Compute the cosine similarity $\cos\theta$ between them.
If two unit-normalized embeddings have cosine similarity $\cos\theta = -1.0$, what is their semantic relationship?
choices: Collinear in the exact same direction
questions.answer: $\cos(180^\circ) = -1.0$: the vectors point in exact opposite directions.

questions.q: Compute the cosine distance $D_{\cos}(\mathbf{u}, \mathbf{v}) = 1 - \cos\theta$ for two orthogonal feature vectors.
Find the scalar projection of vector $\mathbf{a} = [4, 2]^T$ onto the direction of unit vector $\mathbf{u} = [0.6, 0.8]^T$.
In high-dimensional embedding spaces ($D = 1024$), why are two randomly selected vectors almost certainly nearly orthogonal?
choices: The surface area of a high-dimensional hypersphere concentrates near the equator relative to any pole
All high-dimensional vectors have zero norm
The dot product of random Gaussian variables always equals 1
The cosine function approaches infinity as dimension increases
questions.answer: By concentration of measure on the sphere $\mathbf{S}^{D-1}$, almost all mass lies in a thin band around the equator, so $\cos\theta \approx 0$ with high probability.
